title: A novel approach to model traffic on road segments of large-scale urban road networks
author: Jayasinghe, Sano, et al.
materials: TV (i)= Traffic volume of road segment ‘i’,

steps.title: Collect road network data
steps.instruction: Obtain vector road‑centerline GIS data for the study area; each road segment will be a link and each intersection a node.

steps.title: Classify road segments and assign speeds
steps.instruction:
Assign each segment to one of five hierarchy classes and give it the corresponding average speed and Ty value:
- Expressways: 70–100 km/h, Ty = 1/80
- Major arteries: 50–70 km/h, Ty = 1/60
- Minor arteries: 30–50 km/h, Ty = 1/40
- Collectors: 20–30 km/h, Ty = 1/25
- Local roads: <20 km/h, Ty = 1/15

steps.title: Calculate metric distance
steps.instruction: Measure the physical length of each road segment in kilometres; store this as the metric distance MD.

steps.title: Compute path distance
steps.instruction: For every segment calculate PD = Ty × MD (angular‑adjusted metric distance multiplied by the speed‑based factor).

steps.title: Create dual‑graph in sDNA
steps.instruction: Load the road‑centerline layer into the Spatial Design Network Analysis (sDNA) tool and generate a dual graph where road segments become links and intersections become nodes.

steps.title: Set custom distance analysis
steps.instruction: In sDNA choose the “custom distance” analysis option, supply the PD attribute as the distance metric, and set the network influence radius r to 20 km.

steps.title: Calculate centrality measures
steps.instruction: Run sDNA to compute closeness centrality CC(i) and betweenness centrality BC(i) for each segment using the custom distance. Optionally obtain normalized values using equations (4a‑5b) where N is the total number of segments.

steps.title: Fit regression model
steps.instruction: Using observed AADT data (e.g., >7 000 segments from the JICA database), perform linear regression with the form TV(i) = a + b·CC(i) + c·BC(i) to estimate constants a, b, and c.

steps.title: Estimate traffic volumes
steps.instruction: Apply the calibrated equation to every road segment, inserting its CC and BC values to obtain the estimated traffic volume TV(i).

steps.title: Validate model predictions
steps.instruction: Compare the modeled TV(i) with the empirical AADT values for the validation set; compute goodness‑of‑fit statistics (e.g., R²) and report any systematic deviations.
